finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::agent-iterate-ci has no paging net for a failed fixer step, so the same failure mode the review-panel diff now catches still stalls the ci-fix loop silently
evidence: The full text of .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml is supplied, and the claim's reading of it is accurate: the workflow has exactly one job (`iterate`) whose final step is `Run Claude Code` (the step the diff touches, ~line 147), and there is no `if: always()`/`if: failure()` step and no second job that comments or applies `agent:needs-human-review` when that step errors. The only paging path is inside the `Attempts guard` script, which fires only when `failedCi >= MAX_ATTEMPTS`; since a fixer that errors pushes no commit, no new CI run is created, so that counter cannot advance and no further `workflow_run` event fires — the branch stalls without notification. That is the same failure shape the diff explicitly adds `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` to `stalled` for in agent-review-panel.yml (comment at the `stalled` job), so the asymmetry the claim describes is genuinely present. Weighing it down: the diff also adds `allowed_bots` here, removing the specific bot-rejection cause, the pipeline is inert unless `AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED=true`, and the failed run is still visible in the Actions UI — so the impact is a lost safety-net/observability gap on an opt-in loop rather than a functional break.
